core_obligations: One implication is immediate because the new condition is weaker than the corresponding condition in the characterisation of Mittag-Leffler modules (proof lines 21390-21392).

Conversely, given a map from a finitely presented module, lift it through a surjection from a finite free module, apply the hypothesis to get a map to a finitely presented module dominating the lifted one, observe that the kernel of the first map contains the kernel onto the finitely presented module so that the map factors, and compare kernels after tensoring in the displayed square (proof lines 21393-21413).
proof_roadmap: Get the easy direction from the existing characterisation (proof lines 21389-21392).
Factor through the finitely presented module and compare kernels in the square (proof lines 21393-21414).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises Mittag-Leffler modules by the condition that every map from a finite free module is mutually dominating with some map to a finitely presented module (statement lines 21379-21387). The proof does not check the definition directly: one implication is immediate from the existing characterisation, and for the other it lifts a map from a finitely presented module to a finite free one, uses the hypothesis there, notes that the kernel inclusion lets the map factor through the finitely presented module, and compares kernels after tensoring in the displayed commutative square (proof lines 21389-21414). The factoring step that transfers domination from the free module to the finitely presented one is the content. H2.
